description: `hexa analyze --grade` is still only a letter floor, but when it passes with boundary violations it prints a warning that gives the count and names `--exit-code`; `hexa scaffold` fails on any boundary violation; the docs show the gate that is actually enforced.

specs.description: A floor of A passes a tree whose only flaw is one boundary violation, because 100 − 10 = 90 grades A.
specs.given: A source tree with exactly one boundary violation and no other deductions, so it scores 90 and grades A

specs.description: `--grade` alone does not turn into a no-violations gate.
specs.given: A source tree with exactly one boundary violation that grades A
specs.then: The process does not exit 1 because of the violation. Only a grade below the floor can make `--grade` fail.

specs.description: The floor still fails a grade below it.
specs.given: A source tree whose grade is below A
specs.then: The process exits non-zero because the floor is not met

specs.description: `--grade` with any floor below A+ stays a real floor: the pass/fail result depends only on whether the letter meets the floor.
specs.given: Any tree and any floor letter F below A+
specs.then: It exits 0 if and only if the tree's grade is at or above F, whatever the number of boundary violations

specs.description: `--exit-code` is the strict gate and fails on any violation.
specs.given: A source tree with exactly one boundary violation that grades A

specs.description: When a floor passes with a violation, it says so and names the missing flag.
specs.given: A source tree with exactly one boundary violation that grades A
specs.then: The output includes the line `! grade A passes the floor A with 1 boundary violation — --grade is a letter floor; add --exit-code to fail on any`, and the process exits 0

specs.description: A clean tree passes the floor with no warning.
specs.given: A source tree with zero boundary violations that grades A or above
specs.then: The process exits 0 and the output has no 'passes the floor … with … boundary violation' warning and no mention of `--exit-code`

specs.description: The warning counts the violations the score was computed from, not the doubled raw sum.
specs.given: A source tree with exactly one boundary violation, where both the import scan and the deep pass see the same edge
specs.then: The warning says `1 boundary violation` and never `2`

specs.description: No pass with violations is silent.
specs.given: Any tree with N ≥ 1 graded boundary violations whose grade meets floor F
specs.then: It exits 0 and prints exactly one warning that names grade, floor, N, and `--exit-code`

specs.description: When the floor is not met, the run fails rather than printing the 'passes the floor' warning.
specs.given: A tree with boundary violations whose grade is below floor F
specs.then: The process exits non-zero and does not print a 'passes the floor' warning

specs.description: Scaffold fails on one boundary violation even above the floor.
specs.given: A `hexa scaffold` run whose test gate passes and whose result grades A against the default floor A, but has exactly one boundary violation (e.g. a use case importing an adapter)
specs.then: The scaffold fails. It does not print 'is built, gated and graded', and its failure message gives the boundary violation count of 1

specs.description: Scaffold succeeds only when every gate is met.
specs.given: A `hexa scaffold` run whose test gate passes, whose grade is at or above the floor, and which has zero boundary violations
specs.then: The scaffold reports success and the grade line shows 0 boundary violations

specs.description: A lower floor does not excuse a violation in scaffold.
specs.given: A `hexa scaffold` run with a floor below the earned grade (e.g. floor C, grade A), a passing test gate, and one boundary violation
specs.then: The scaffold fails because of the boundary violation

specs.description: Zero violations does not excuse a failed test gate or a missed floor.
specs.given: A `hexa scaffold` run with zero boundary violations where either the test gate fails or the grade is below the floor

specs.description: The scaffold's pass condition is the conjunction of all three gates.
specs.given: Any scaffold result with test outcome T, grade G, floor F and boundary violation count V
specs.then: It succeeds if and only if T passed, G ≥ F and V = 0

specs.description: Every CI gate shown in the docs includes `--exit-code`.
specs.when: They show the CI gate for `hexa analyze`
specs.then: The command shown is `--grade A --exit-code` (or a floor plus `--exit-code`)

specs.description: No doc presents `--grade A` alone as the CI gate.
specs.when: They are searched for a `hexa analyze` gate invocation
specs.then: None of them presents `--grade A` without `--exit-code` as the gate that blocks violations

specs.description: The docs describe the scaffold gate the way it is enforced.
specs.then: They describe it as 'grade earned and no import crosses a boundary', not as reaching a grade letter only
